clue.text: Lavengro'd have beer in this Lakeland beauty-spot

parts.note: Lavengro is the novel by George Borrow, so Lavengro'd stands for its author: Borrow'd, i.e. Borrow would
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: The author of a classic travel book would have enjoyed a pint in this lovely corner of the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: Lavengro (1851) is George Borrow's semi-autobiographical novel, so 'Lavengro'd have beer' reads 'Borrow'd ale'. BORROWDALE is a valley in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowdale is a celebrated valley of the Cumbrian fells, a scenic spot in the Lake District.

clue.text: Fish follows love-note, looking flirtatious

indicators.note: follows puts the fish after love and note

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
G is a musical note
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish swims after a romantic letter, eyeing it coyly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-note' looks like a billet-doux, but splits into O (love) and G (a note).
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling means eyeing someone amorously, a flirtatious sort of looking.

clue.text: Gathers together for games of course on horseback

parts.note: rounds are games of golf played over a course
up means riding, as a jockey is said to be up

explanation.surface: Collecting people for golf matches while mounted.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey who is riding a horse is said to be 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up is to collect scattered people or animals into one place.

clue.text: As an astronaut felt — lacking importance?

explanation.surface: An astronaut floating in orbit feels insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: In orbit an astronaut has no apparent heaviness; figuratively, something without weight carries no significance.

clue.text: Dreadful putting so many in a small compass

indicators.note: to compass is to surround, so the small phrase encloses the other letters

parts.note: a wee is Scots for a small
taken as written
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: Something frightful about cramming a crowd into a tiny space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' is the verb to encircle: A WEE goes round SO and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its older sense means inspiring awe or dread, terrible.

clue.text: Times royalty like

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
as means like

explanation.surface: The newspaper fond of the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are periods of history, ages or epochs.

clue.text: Frank won't broadcast shouldn't be attacked by enemy

parts.note: open means frank or candid

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of won't are scrambled

explanation.surface: A candid presenter refuses to go on air about not being bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: An open town is one declared undefended in war, so by convention it should not be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the laws of war an undefended settlement is declared exempt from bombardment.

clue.text: Where Thames-side residents enjoy their days?.

definitions.text: Where Thames-side residents enjoy their days?.

parts.words: Where Thames-side residents enjoy their days?.
parts.note: every dog has its day, so a riverside spot named for canines is where they enjoy their days

explanation.surface: Where Londoners living by the river spend their leisure time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district on a loop of the Thames in east London; the proverb 'every dog has its day' supplies the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula in east London is bounded by the Thames, and its name suggests a home for hounds having their day.

clue.text: Spirit given to drink brought back uproar

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: brought back tells us the word for drink is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Somebody's liquor and a returned drink end in a row at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion, a synonym for an uproar.

clue.text: False complaint made by four in employment

parts.note: an ill is an ailment or complaint

indicators.note: in places the numeral for four within the word for employment

parts.note: use means employment, as in putting something to use
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bogus grievance concocted by a group of four at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusive means deceptive or unreal, close in sense to false.

clue.text: Anxious uncertainty in S American writers' quarter

parts.note: taken as written, a single letter in the clue
pens are writing implements, so writers
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Nervous tension felt in some South American literary district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S American' looks like South American, but S is just a letter and American gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense state of waiting without knowing the outcome.

clue.text: Pay not starting for a long time

indicators.note: not starting means the word for pay loses its first letter

parts.note: wages are pay

explanation.surface: Wages withheld for a long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is informal for a very long period, as in 'I waited ages'.

clue.text: Mid-August feast that is taken for granted?

explanation.surface: A summer church festival that nobody questions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Feast of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary falls on 15 August.
explanation.definitionFit: The church festival of 15 August marks Mary taken up to heaven; also a supposition accepted without proof.

clue.text: Wood took wild-fowl, the beast

parts.note: timber is wood

indicators.note: wild tells us the letters of fowl are scrambled

explanation.surface: In the woods, a hunter bagged some wild birds and then the creature appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild-fowl' reads as one word, but 'wild' is the anagram signal on FOWL, giving WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber wolf is the grey wolf of North America, a wild animal.

clue.text: Prayers bring items' on, menu around at one

indicators.note: around means the menu dishes go round the other letters

parts.note: entrees are dishes listed on a menu
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pleading for things on the bill of fare at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'items on menu' without the stray apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Entreaties are earnest pleas or requests, akin to prayers.

clue.text: Pole gets more liberal supply of needlework

parts.note: S, south, is one of the Earth's poles
ampler means more generous or liberal

explanation.surface: A Polish person obtains a more generous allowance of sewing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person but gives S for the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is an embroidered panel showing off stitches, a classic piece of embroidery.

clue.text: Chinese, example of"'tongues in trees"

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's forest about talking trees, applied to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongues in trees' is from As You Like It; the answer is both a language (tongue) and a citrus tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main Chinese language and also the small orange tree, so both a tongue and a tree.

clue.text: Emperor swallowed hurried port in Italy

indicators.note: swallowed puts the word for hurried inside the emperor's name

parts.note: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A ruler gulped something down in haste at an Italian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OTRANTO is a port in Apulia on the heel of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Otranto is a coastal town and harbour in south-eastern Italy.

clue.text: Western Asian member has written letter to Scot

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member
en is the letter N written out as a word
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A man from the Caucasus has written to a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written letter' means a letter spelt out as a word: EN for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia lies in western Asia, so an Armenian is a person from there.

clue.text: Eccentric poet lad found in pond?

definitions.text: Eccentric poet lad found in pond?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of poet and lad are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd young versifier discovered in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a quirky little 'lad' found in a pond is a frog larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog larva is a pond creature, a little wriggler found in water.

clue.text: Various carols used in pit, for music practice

indicators.note: used in places the rearranged carols inside the word for pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of carols arranged in a different order

explanation.surface: Miners singing assorted carols underground as a musical exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners drill scales, and the minor scale is one standard exercise for practising an instrument.

clue.text: Space traveller must always regulate speed, initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: An astronaut should keep a careful eye on velocity at all times.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is a planet, forever travelling in its orbit through space.

clue.text: Go about two

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pair is two

explanation.surface: Leave with a couple of others.
explanation.walkthrough: To repair to a place is an old way of saying to go there.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair in the sense 'betake oneself' means to head somewhere.

clue.text: A little waterfall should not spoil the view in Happy Valley

definitions.text: A little waterfall should not spoil the view in Happy Valley

parts.words: A little waterfall should not spoil the view in Happy Valley
parts.note: a single drop of water falling from a weeping eye is a tiny waterfall, and in a happy place nobody should be crying

explanation.surface: A small cascade must not ruin the scenery of a pleasant valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shed from the eye in sorrow is like a miniature waterfall, out of place where all is happy.

clue.text: Some insertion for a special-file?

indicators.note: some insertion means a part sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bit of extra matter slipped into a special folder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse metal tool for smoothing wood, a type of file.

clue.text: First said about one drink

indicators.note: about means the word for said goes round the other pieces

parts.note: oral means spoken or said
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: The first thing anyone said concerned a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means earliest or initial, the first of its kind.

clue.text: Supposes work is to include quarters

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: to include means the word is holds the compass letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written
N and E are two quarters of the compass, north and east

explanation.surface: A thinker reckons the job must take in lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or state a view, much as one supposes.

clue.text: Joke for many -among Tyler's supporters

indicators.note: among places the letter for many inside the word for Tyler's followers

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, so his followers were the peasantry
L is fifty in Roman numerals, a large number, so many

explanation.surface: A jest that went down well with the crowds backing a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt in 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light humorous remark, a gentle joke.
